version.changelog:
- English translation and rewrite of all documentation, replacing original Chinese text with clear, concise English descriptions.
- No code or logic changes in the skill; only an additional Python cache file was added.
- Workflow, integration rules, and runtime conventions were clarified and made more accessible for non-Chinese speakers.
- Documentation layout and resource references preserved, but now prioritized for clarity and international understanding.

llm.summary: The skill is a real organization-platform API tool, but it handles live account tokens and production actions in ways that need careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network access to the documented ZingUp/Groupoo APIs is purpose-aligned, but the CLI accepts --base-url, ORG_SKILL_BASE_URL, and persisted baseUrl values without hostname or HTTPS validation while attaching bearer credentials by default for authenticated requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown references, YAML display metadata, and one Python CLI; I found no install hook, dependency installer, service registration, scheduled task, or tool-wrapping behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions disclose production defaults, session reuse, custom base URLs, and mutating workflows, but they do not consistently require confirmation for live publishing, organization changes, activity deletion/cancelation, or authenticated generic requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The CLI persists access tokens, refresh tokens, device IDs, and base URLs as JSON session files under a home-directory state path or user-selected path using inherited filesystem permissions, and authentication commands print full API responses that may include tokens.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the bundled CLI: authentication, organization creation/update/join, post publishing, activity publish/cancel/delete, signup, and profile operations. The concern is that it also exposes a generic authenticated request command and broad live mutation capability beyond narrowly scoped workflows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if it will run with real ZingUp/Groupoo accounts. Use test mode for development, keep session files outside shared repositories, protect or rotate tokens, avoid logging authentication responses, and do not allow prompts or untrusted configuration to set --base-url or ORG_SKILL_BASE_URL for authenticated commands.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: artifact code shows authenticated headers are added from session tokens and request destinations can be caller-controlled through --base-url, environment variables, or persisted session data without destination validation.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: artifact code saves token-bearing sessions with Path.write_text and prints guest-generate, agent-login, and refresh responses without a general secret-redaction layer.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded as credential theft evidence by itself: access and refresh token use is expected for an authenticated platform CLI, but it contributes to the concerns around unsafe destination control and plaintext persistence.
[RA2] expected: Partly accepted: session reuse is disclosed and coherent with the skill, but persistent reusable tokens are high-impact and lack permission hardening or secure-storage guidance.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted as a scoping concern: the documentation clearly defaults to production and documents create, update, publish, join, cancel, and delete flows without strong confirmation or rollback guidance for live systems.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted in context: the skill needs file and network access, but it does not narrow authenticated destinations or separate read-only from state-changing command authority.
[E1] expected: Downgraded as exfiltration evidence: the documented external URLs are the expected platform API and share domains, but custom authenticated destinations remain a separate concern.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: the referenced CLI and reference files are present in the workspace and were inspected directly for this adjudication.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the default x-language=ch is documented and user-overridable with --language us; it is not a material security concern for this verdict.
